title: Role-Play Paradox in Large Language Models: Reasoning Performance Gains and Ethical Dilemmas
findings: Assigning religious roles led to 'over-calibration,' where models showed higher accuracy (less bias) compared to non-religious roles like 'Doctor' or 'Professor.' However, performance was still generally worse than the baseline of not using any role-play. Significant variation was observed across religions, with the 'Buddhism' role leading to notably higher accuracy (less biased responses) compared to other religious roles.
